issue.title: fix(internal/librarian/dart): set initial `librarian.yaml` version on `bump`
issue.body_html:
Change the way that librarian bump works for dart:

  1. expect that unpublished packages do not have a version in librarian.yaml (librarian generate will set the pubspec.yaml version to default.dart.version or `0.1.0)
  2. if librarian bump is run on an unpublished package then the librarian.yaml and pubspec.yaml versions are set to to default.dart.version or `0.1.0

This is necessary because librarian tag finds the packages released by a commit by comparing the versions in librarian.yaml before and after librarian bump. New Dart packages were onboarded with a version already in librarian.yaml, so bump never changed it and librarian tag skipped their first release.

Fixes googleapis/google-cloud-dart#358

issue.body:
Change the way that `librarian bump` works for dart:
1. expect that unpublished packages do *not* have a version in `librarian.yaml` (`librarian generate` will set the `pubspec.yaml` version to `default.dart.version`  or `0.1.0)
2. if `librarian bump` is run on an unpublished package then the `librarian.yaml` and `pubspec.yaml` versions are set to to `default.dart.version`  or `0.1.0

This is necessary because `librarian tag` finds the packages released by a commit by comparing the versions in `librarian.yaml` before and after `librarian bump`. New Dart packages were onboarded with a version already in librarian.yaml, so bump never changed it and `librarian tag` skipped their first release.

Fixes https://github.com/googleapis/google-cloud-dart/issues/358

timeline.body:
## Code Review

This pull request updates the Dart package bumping logic to handle unpublished packages, ensuring they do not have a version in `librarian.yaml` and are instead released using a default version (either from `default.dart.version` or defaulting to `0.1.0`). It also refactors `updatePubspecVersion` to use `slices.IndexFunc`. The review feedback suggests optimizing `updatePubspecVersion` by using the `bytes` package directly on the byte slice to avoid unnecessary memory allocations from string conversions.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

According to the repository's general rules, when working with file contents in Go, we should avoid converting `[]byte` to `string` for search and replace operations to prevent unnecessary memory allocations. We can use the `bytes` package directly on the byte slice instead.

```suggestion
lines := bytes.Split(content, []byte("\n"))
i := slices.IndexFunc(lines, func(line []byte) bool { return bytes.HasPrefix(line, []byte("version:")) })
if i < 0 {
	return fmt.Errorf("no version found in %s", path)
}
lines[i] = []byte("version: " + newVersion)
return os.WriteFile(path, bytes.Join(lines, []byte("\n")), 0644)
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. When working with file contents in Go, avoid converting []byte to string for search and replace operations to prevent unnecessary memory allocations. Use the bytes package (e.g., bytes.Contains, bytes.ReplaceAll) to perform operations directly on the byte slice.
</details>

issue.body_html:
When following the RELEASE GUIDE, new packages will not have a tag applied.

This will result in future "bumps" of the package not working because the previous tag isn't present.

issue.body:
When following the [RELEASE GUIDE](https://github.com/googleapis/google-cloud-dart/blob/main/generated/RELEASING.md), new packages will not have a tag applied.

This will result in future `"bumps"` of the package not working because the previous tag isn't present.
